text:
Alex: quick question — hitting a weird API contract edge with generation + stop sequences + max_tokens. Observed finish_reason flip and missing logprobs when we truncate. Repro below, can someone confirm intended behavior?

Mia: can you paste the exact request/response payload you saw?

Alex: sure — minimal repro: 
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-1\",
  \"prompt\": \"Q: Hello\\nA:\",
  \"max_tokens\": 1,
  \"stop\": [\"\\n\"],
  \"temperature\": 0.0,
  \"top_p\": 1.0,
  \"logprobs\": 5
}
```
Response snip: 
```json
{
  \"choices\": [
    {
      \"text\": \" the\",
      \"logprobs\": null,
      \"finish_reason\": \"stop\"
    }
  ]
}
```
We expected deterministic token + logprobs + finish_reason set to \"length\" when max_tokens hit. Instead finish_reason was \"stop\" and logprobs null.

Devon: hmm. Two things: (1) history: older runtime used to map a max_tokens cap to \"length\" finish_reason. If it also matched a stop sequence at the same time the mapping could be ambiguous. (2) logprobs null suggests we followed a fast-path that omitted scoring for argmax path. Any chance temp==0 short-circuit ran and dropped logprobs?

Sasha: that matches my suspicion — our sampler short-circuits at temp==0 to an argmax-only code path for perf; historically we still computed logprobs for that path, but a recent refactor accidentally skipped the scoring step when nucleus/top_p codepath was pruned.

Mia: related Q: if temperature==0, should top_p be considered at all? My mental model: temp=0 => deterministic argmax, top_p should be ignored. Does API contract state that?

Devon: it wasn't explicitly spelled out in the public API docs. Implementation historically did: if temp==0 then ignore top_p/typical sampling and go argmax. But some integrations set top_p<1 and relied on deterministic behavior anyway. We should document and enforce.

Jordan: runtime note: we also recently changed finish_reason enum to include \"length\" (truncated by max_tokens), \"stop\" (matched stop seq), and \"eos\" (model emitted EOS). There was a mapping mismatch in the control-plane that converted \"eos\" -> \"stop\" in the JSON surface which could explain the flip. Will investigate.

Alex: good to know. Another oddity: when max_tokens truncates mid-token (tokenization boundary), sometimes choices.text ends mid-word and logprobs length != tokens length. That breaks our eval harness expecting arrays aligned. Can we guarantee alignment?

Sasha: we should absolutely guarantee tokens/logprobs align with the returned text/tokens arrays. Truncating by max_tokens must still return scoring for the last emitted token. Bug likely from the same short-circuit: we stopped after selecting token but before scoring metadata writeout.

Devon: proposed fixes: (A) sampler: ensure argmax path still computes logprobs when logprobs requested; (B) runtime: canonicalize finish_reason to legacy-ish behavior: max_tokens -> \"length\", stop match -> \"stop\"; (C) API docs: explicitly state temp==0 implies deterministic and top_p ignored (or top_p treated as 1).

Mia: +1 to adding a compatibility note. For backward compatibility, product asks we don't break older SDKs that parse finish_reason. If we change semantics, we should add a control-plane shim that maps new enum -> legacy values unless client opts into new enum via header. Thoughts?

Jordan: I prefer fixing semantics and keeping the public mapping stable: if truncated by max_tokens return \"length\" (same string), if stop seq matched before length return \"stop\". Avoid an extra header. If we add a new \"eos\" value we can use it internally but not expose it until next major. Simpler to keep the surface stable.

Alex: sounds reasonable. Small ask: can we also make an explicit note that when stop sequences overlap token boundaries the behavior is defined as \"stop matches if full string matches tokenization/decoded output\" (i.e., match against decoded text not token sequence)? That avoids ambiguity in clients.

Sasha: yes, define stop matching as on decoded UTF-8 output after detokenization. Add test cases for multi-byte and whitespace-edge stops.

Devon: I'm going to open a small runtime PR: enforce top_p=1 when temp==0 (sampler-level), compute logprobs on argmax path when logprobs requested, and adjust finish_reason mapping so max_tokens->\"length\". Will add unit + integration tests for stop crossing token boundaries.

Jordan: I'll review. Also please add a regression test for the eval harness that serializes tokens/logprobs arrays and validates alignment.

Alex: thanks — that should buy us determinism for evals. Any ETA?

Devon: aiming EOD tomorrow for the PR, staging rollout Thursday.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: staging/runtime-sampler-fix -> eta 2026-03-20 03:00 UTC :rocket:

Mia: perfect. After deploy, Alex can re-run the repro and confirm logprobs + finish_reason stable. Alex, ping here when done and we'll close the ticket.

Alex: will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Jordan: one more note for docs/SDK: add a small snippet explaining deterministic mode (temp==0) and that top_p will be ignored. Also call out finish_reason mapping in the migration guide.

Sasha: added to backlog, I'll slot into next docs sprint.

Alex: closing loop — appreciate the quick triage.
